text:
Maria Chen: Heads up — after the kernel selector rollout to kernel-v2.4 we see a sharp drop in prefix KV cache hit rate for eu-west-1. baseline was ~82% this morning, now ~49%. Latency tail up ~18ms p95. Noticed this ~10:02Z.

ops-bot: deploy finished: kernel-select v2.4 -> rollout at 2026-03-16T10:58:12Z (canary eu-west-1 then global).

Kevin Park: Ack. Can you paste the region breakdown and timeframe slices?

Maria Chen: Sure — quick slices from observability: 
- global prefix_hit_rate: 76% -> 70% (minor)
- eu-west-1 prefix_hit_rate: 82% -> 49% (major)
- us-west-2 prefix_hit_rate: 80% -> 78% (small)
- replication lag (kv replication ms median): 18ms -> 310ms in eu region right after rollout
- p95 request latency (token gen): eu went 42ms -> 60ms

Sanjay Patel: That replication lag jump smells like key normalization/hash mismatch + replication storms. Any recent PRs touching kv keying?

Maria Chen: Yes — PR #4523 changed prefix keying to include seq_len_bucket and model_variant for better cache separation. It also flipped trimming of trailing whitespace to run after normalization instead of before. I worried it might change keys for in-flight prefixes.

Ada Gomez: I eyeballed a sample: same user prompt yields different keys pre/post-change — seq_len_bucket added a different bucket because we changed bucket boundaries from 64->128 in the same PR. So identical textual prefixes now map to different keys on the primary and cached replicas for short windows during replication.

Kevin Park: Oof. So two effects: (1) kernel selection change changed batching heuristics and increased simultaneous writes to kv primaries, (2) key normalization change made cache misses incompatible across older entries, triggers hot writes/replication. Combined produced replication lag and miss spike.

Maria Chen: Repro script attached (quick local):
```
# sample repro (uses test harness)
for p in $(seq 1 2000); do
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" -d '{"prompt":"hello world"}' https://canary.redwood.internal/generate >/dev/null &
done
wait
```
Logs show many 404s from kv shard clients followed by heavy write QPS.

Sanjay Patel: Interesting — latency-aware kernel selection reduced batch_window_ms from 12 -> 6 to favor latency. That likely increased small-batch churn and made prefix writes less amortized. Combined with key mismatch = storm.

Ada Gomez: Quick mitigation proposals: 
1) Roll back key normalization change (revert PR #4523) in eu canary only.
2) Increase replication throttle / backoff to avoid leader overload (temporal fix).
3) Reintroduce prefix canonicalization that neutralizes seq_len_bucket differences for the next 48h.
4) Re-run canary with batch_window_ms bumped to 10ms to reduce write churn.

Kevin Park: I prefer 1 + 4 for immediate mitigation. Rolling back normalization in one region is easiest and quick. Canary rollback?

deploy-bot: rollback request queued: revert PR #4523 (eu canary). Estimated time to revert: ~4 minutes.

ops-bot: rollback started at 2026-03-16T11:05:10Z. will post status.

Maria Chen: Also starting a regional priming job to pre-warm top-10k prefixes surfaced by the last 24h high-traffic traces. Script will run at 11:20Z in eu to re-populate caches once keys match.

Kevin Park: After rollback, let's temporarily set kernel.batch_window_ms=10 for eu and monitor. Where's that config?

Ada Gomez: running config change: 
```
PATCH /api/v1/runtime/configs/eu-west-1
{
  "kernel.batch_window_ms": "10",
  "kv.replication_backoff_ms": "200"
}
```

ops-bot: config change applied for eu-west-1 at 2026-03-16T11:08:54Z (kernel.batch_window_ms=10, kv.replication_backoff_ms=200).

deploy-bot: revert completed: PR #4523 reverted in eu canary at 11:09:40Z.

Maria Chen: Early numbers 3 minutes post-rollback: eu prefix_hit_rate climbed 49% -> 71%, replication lag median back to 25ms, p95 latency down ~10ms. Still below 82 baseline but trending.

Sanjay Patel: Good. Plan next: 
- Hold kernel-v2.4 global rollout until we resolve keying design.
- Open a postmortem PR that includes test harness for key canonicalization across bucket boundary changes.
- Add synthetic priming during rollouts: pre-warm top N prefixes per region before switching keying rules.

Action items:
- Maria: run 24h priming job and collect top-10k prefixes (in progress).
- Kevin: coordinate a keying design review, propose a compatible schema that is forward/backward tolerant (avoid seq_len_bucket in key or encode it as tag not in the canonical key).
- Ada: add regression test to eval pipeline that runs small-batch hammer to ensure no replication storms.

Ada Gomez: I'll file the follow-up PRs — starting with a compatibility shim that maps old keys to new when seq_len_bucket boundary change detected. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/4580 (draft).

Maria Chen: We'll leave the kernel.batch_window_ms=10 for eu for 6 hours, then reassess. If stable, we can gradually re-enable v2.4 in canary with the shim.

Kevin Park: Also add a metric alert: if regional prefix_hit_rate drops >15% in 5m window after any kernel/config change, auto-rollback trigger (ops playbook).

ops-bot: noted and opened ticket RUNTIME-884: auto-rollback threshold rule.

Sanjay Patel: Nice. Quick note for the postmortem: include flamegraphs from kernel before/after, kv client traces showing replication bursts, and the small-batch QPS histograms.

Maria Chen: Will collect artifacts and link here. Thanks all — nice fast follow. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: monitoring: eu prefix_hit_rate 71% -> 73% over the last 2m. Keeping watch.
